quotes.text: Telemetry is a record of repeated measurements over time. One reading has limited meaning on its own, but the sequence tells you how the machine behaved during a real production run.
quotes.speaker: Mirko Peters
quotes.why: Defines telemetry crisply as a sequence-dependent production record.

quotes.text: A disconnected gateway tells you that cloud visibility has changed. That's enough to trigger an investigation. It isn't enough to write the production story.
quotes.speaker: Mirko Peters
quotes.why: Draws the line between a connection event and a production conclusion.

quotes.text: Event Grid is a notification fabric, not an industrial historian. It is built to distribute notices in near real time, so reactive systems can start their own work.
quotes.speaker: Mirko Peters
quotes.why: Positions Event Grid precisely against data storage and history use cases.

quotes.text: Good industrial architecture protects attention. It keeps the continuous record available for analysis, and it raises a response signal when a defined condition needs a response.
quotes.speaker: Mirko Peters
quotes.why: Summarises the design principle of separating records from response signals.

quotes.text: A connected gateway proves one narrow fact that gateway can talk to IoT Hub. It doesn't prove the machine is healthy, the PLC link works, or the line produced good parts.
quotes.speaker: Mirko Peters
quotes.why: Warns against treating cloud connection state as machine uptime.

takeaways: Route continuous machine telemetry through IoT Hub message routing into streams and storage, because its value depends on preserved sequence, retention and independent consumers.
Use Event Grid for discrete lifecycle and condition events that should start work, but design handlers to be idempotent and to check current state since delivery is at-least-once and unordered.
A device disconnect only proves lost cloud visibility; production impact must be confirmed with MES, asset model and ERP context before anyone re-plans a work order.
hook: Manufacturing teams often call every sensor reading an event and end up with noisy workflows or buried alerts. This episode follows one press line to show architects and OT/IT engineers when Azure IoT Hub message routing fits and when Event Grid does. You learn how to keep the production record intact while still triggering the right response fast.
